title: Hypothesis v1
description:
A typed, falsifiable security hypothesis in the hypothesis-and-experiment
ledger (lib/hypothesis.py). One JSON object per line in
<workspace>/.lab/hypotheses.jsonl. The ledger is append-only; the status
field advances via status-transition experiments (see experiment-v1), never
by mutating an existing line.

Design lineage (transferable mechanisms, reimplemented not copied):
  - Shannon's `.refine()`-pinned referential IDs: every experiment/finding
    MUST reference an existing hypothesis_id; a hallucinated or duplicate id
    is rejected with a retryable structured error listing the valid ids.
  - Shannon's exploitation_queue taxonomy: falsifiable, sink-aware format
    forcing the author to name the sink, the mutation, the expected-safe
    result, the violating signal, and the minimum confirmation that would
    DISCONFIRM the hypothesis. Scanner output enters only as an unverified
    hypothesis, never a verdict.
  - PentestAgent's decomposed exploitability rubric feeds the deterministic
    ranking (primitive_leverage x scope_safety x novelty x impact_potential
    x (1 - known_dead_end_penalty)); see lib/hypothesis.rank().
  - XBOW's agent/validator split: a hypothesis is a CLAIM; the lab's
    evidence gate (not the authoring agent) decides whether it is confirmed.

Required fields (the falsifiable core):
  schema, hypothesis_id, workspace_id, engagement, invariant, surface,
  preconditions, mutation, expected_safe, violation_signal, minimum_confirmation,
  disconfirming_controls, primitive_leverage, status, scope, provenance, ts.

status transitions (ranker/agent reads; the ledger never deletes):
  unverified -> testing -> confirmed | disconfirmed | superseded
  A scanner/tool finding always enters as unverified. The ranker will not
  surface a confirmed hypothesis unless at least one experiment/finding record
  (experiment-v1.schema.json) references it with a corroborating result.

hypothesis_id.description:
Stable identifier. Convention: 'hyp-<uuid4>'. This is the referential key
experiments/finding records pin to (the .refine() gate).

workspace_id.description:
UUID of the workspace from <workspace>/.lab/workspace.json, or null when
the workspace has no workspace.json. Immutable provenance — once written,
the ledger never changes this field.

engagement.description:
Engagement name (e.g. 'bounty-notion', 'ctf-example', 'cve-log4j').
Immutable provenance; ties the hypothesis to a scope file.

invariant.description:
The security invariant the hypothesis claims is violated. One falsifiable
sentence naming what SHOULD hold (the expected-safe property), so the
experiment can disconfirm it. Example: 'A user may only read objects owned
by their workspace.'
examples: A user may only read objects owned by their workspace.

surface.description:
The attack surface / component under test. Concrete enough to dedupe
against: endpoint, file:line, function, parameter, binary, etc.

preconditions.description:
Actor/resource preconditions that must hold before the mutation. Captures
the multi-account / stateful setup that IDOR and business-logic bugs require
(the gap the competitor report flags for the whole field).

actor.description:
The actor performing the mutation (e.g. 'user-A (low-priv)', 'attacker
unauthenticated', 'fuzz harness').

target_resource.description:
The resource being acted on (e.g. 'object owned by user-B', 'endpoint
requiring admin'). null when the mutation does not target a specific
resource.

auth_state.description:
Required auth/session state (e.g. 'valid JWT for user-A', 'no session').
null when auth is not relevant.

environment.description:
Environment preconditions (e.g. 'target on localhost:8080', 'Docker
sandbox with --network none'). null when not applicable.

mutation.description:
The mutation/test action the hypothesis says will violate the invariant.
Concrete enough that an experiment can replay it (a witness payload or
request shape). Names the sink where applicable.
examples: Submit order confirm step skipping the payment step

expected_safe.description:
What the system should return/do when the invariant HOLDS (the control
outcome). The experiment compares the observed result to this.
examples: Order remains in 'awaiting_payment' state; confirm endpoint rejects

violation_signal.description:
The observable signal that would indicate the invariant is VIOLATED. Must
be machine-checkable where possible (status code, body marker, state diff,
OOB callback, crash). This is the oracle — the agent's self-report is not
sufficient; the experiment must capture this signal independently.
examples: 200 OK with body containing user-B's marker AND owner_user_id == user-B
GET /api/v1/orders/<id> returns state=confirmed with confirmed_at set
interactsh callback observed within 30s of payload

minimum_confirmation.description:
The minimum evidence that would CONFIRM the violation (the bar to move
status to 'confirmed'). Names the independent signal — never 'the agent
said so'. Mirrors XBOW's deterministic validator + canary SHA256 + OOB
callback proof ladder.
examples: Cross-session request returns user-B's controlled marker AND owner_user_id verified as user-B's (not just a 200).
Replay against a fresh instance produces the same state transition; pre/post hashes match the fixture.

disconfirming_controls.description:
Controls or alternative explanations the experiment must rule out before
claiming confirmation (the disconfirmation gate). Forces the author to
name what would make a positive signal a false positive (cached response,
WAF rewrite, shared account, test fixture). Empty string when none apply.
examples: Response is not cached (Cache-Control: no-store); user-A and user-B are distinct accounts, not the same session.

primitive_leverage.description:
Coarse leverage category feeding the deterministic ranker
(lib.hypothesis.rank). Maps to PentestAgent's impact ladder.
- state_changing: 1.0 (writes/creates/deletes/escalates)
- read_only: 0.5 (reads data but does not change state)
- theoretical: 0.1 (no demonstrated primitive yet)

status.description:
Lifecycle status. Scanner/tool findings always enter as 'unverified'.
Transitions: unverified -> testing -> confirmed | disconfirmed | superseded.
A hypothesis is 'confirmed' ONLY when an experiment record
(experiment-v1.schema.json) references it with result='corroborating' and
the minimum_confirmation bar is met. The ledger never deletes; superseded
keeps the line for audit.

scope.description:
Immutable scope/workspace provenance. The ranker REJECTS records where a
target is involved and scope_checked is not true — preserving the lab's
default-deny scope gate (AGENTS.md). A target is 'involved' when
scope.target is a non-empty URL/host (source-only review may set target
to '' and scope_checked to false).

scope_checked.description:
True iff lab-scope was run against scope.target and returned 0 (in-scope).
The ranker rejects target-bearing records with scope_checked=false.

target.description:
The target URL/host/path the hypothesis is about. Empty string when the
hypothesis is source-only or abstract (no live target).

engagement_scope_ref.description:
Reference to the scope snapshot used (engagement file path, or 'none' for
source-only). Immutable provenance — ties the record to the scope file it
was validated against.

provenance.description:
Who/what produced this hypothesis. Scanner/tool findings enter as
unverified hypotheses with provenance.source = the tool name; the lab never
treats a tool finding as a verdict.

source.description:
Origin of the hypothesis. 'manual' for agent-authored; a tool name
('semgrep','nuclei','httpx','browser','fuzz','strix') for scanner/tool
findings. Tool-sourced records always enter as status='unverified'.

agent.description:
Agent name (e.g. 'opencode', 'claude') or the tool name when the tool
produced the record directly.

tool_rule_id.description:
For tool-sourced records: the rule id (semgrep check_id, nuclei template
id). null for manual hypotheses.

raw_ref.description:
Path to the raw tool finding kept for provenance (e.g.
'evidence/recon/semgrep.sarif'). The raw payload is never trusted; it is
kept so a reviewer can re-inspect. null for manual hypotheses.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the hypothesis was recorded.

evidence_refs.description:
Evidence file references that support the hypothesis (paths under
<workspace>/evidence/). Empty for a fresh unverified hypothesis; grows as
experiments are recorded.

tags.description:
Free-form tags for query filtering (e.g. ['idor','authz','business-logic']).
Not used for ranking.

examples.invariant: A user may only read objects owned by their workspace.
examples.violation_signal: 200 OK with body containing user-B's marker AND owner_user_id == user-B
examples.minimum_confirmation: Cross-session request returns user-B's controlled marker AND owner_user_id verified as user-B's (not just a 200).
examples.disconfirming_controls: Response is not cached (Cache-Control: no-store); user-A and user-B are distinct accounts, not the same session.

examples.invariant: The parser rejects inputs larger than the configured max length.

preconditions.environment: Docker sandbox with --network none, ASan build

examples.mutation: Feed an input of length 2^20 with a length prefix claiming 2^16.
examples.violation_signal: Heap buffer overflow reported by ASan (crash with stack trace at parse_length:88).
examples.minimum_confirmation: Replay of the crash input against a fresh ASan build reproduces the ASan report at the same source location.
